newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FORECAST-Westpac H1 earnings seen rising.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Westpac H1 earnings seen rising.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp is expected to post stronger first half earnings on Wednesday, the bank's performance seen aided by lower costs and higher income from fees, banking analysts said on Monday.
Last month, Westpac managing director Bob Joss said he expected the bank's earning for the first half ended March 31 to exceed the previous first half result of A$565 million.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast the bank's half year net profit after abnormals but before preference dividend will rise to between A$595 million and A$620 million.

"They (Westpac) have been doing a fair bit of work over the last few years on their costs. They are getting themselves into a better cost position now," Colonial Investment Management's senior investment manager, Martin Hickling told Reuters.
On the downside, analysts said the bank's earnings growth could be restricted by increased competition in the home loans market where there have been sharp cuts in lending margins.
At Westpac's annual meeting in January, chairman John Uhrig told shareholders competition in the lending market was expected to remain intense.
In the past two years, Australian banks have been squeezed by non-bank lenders, who, funded by the wholesale money markets, have cut mortgage rates, forcing banks to follow.
Analysts said another focus was the bank's income from fees, an area seen as crucial if the big banks are to offset the effect of tighter margins.

Macquarie Equities bank analyst Graham Maloney said Westpac had not done as well as National Australia Bank Ltd and Commonwealth Bank of Australia in building market share in the home loan market, but he said Westpac was focusing on growth by acquisition.

"Westpac has been concentrating more on their acquisitions than they have on just organic growth at this stage. They want to get all that in place and see what they need to do to get more organic growth," he said.
Westpac is currently bidding for Victorian-based regional bank, Bank of Melbourne Ltd.
The A$1.435 billion takeover offer was launched just before the release of the Wallis enquiry into Australia's financial system which recommended mergers be allowed between Australia's largest banks.
The bid is still awaiting approval by anti-monopolies watchdog the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC).
Westpac has said the takeover is integral to its plans to strengthen its presence in several key markets.
The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) has launched an inquiry into unusual trading of Bank of Melbourne shares on the eve of last month's bid.
